# My plan for this year

*[Reasoning in my own voice — first person, middle-school-educated farmer]*

Let me think about this year. I've got 50 mu to manage, and at home it's just me, my wife, and my elderly mother. So family labor is really just two of us — my mother helps with small jobs around the yard but can't do field work anymore. That's the thing I have to keep in mind for everything I decide.

My main crop is stevia now. I started switching over some years back when the buyers came around offering contracts — the price is steadier than cotton and you don't have to sit picking for weeks. I've still kept about 15 mu in cotton because I don't want to put all my eggs in one basket, and honestly cotton is what I grew up farming. If the stevia price drops or the contract changes, I still have something.

**For the stevia (35 mu):**
The plants are already established from last year — stevia is perennial, I don't need to replant the whole field, just fill in gaps where plants died over winter. I'll need to cut and dry leaves 2 or 3 times through the season. First cutting around late June, second in August, maybe a third in September if it keeps growing well.

For fertilizer, stevia is a leaf crop so it wants nitrogen. The extension guy at the agricultural station said 18 kg N per mu but I usually put down closer to 22 kg because my ground isn't that rich and I've seen the yield suffer when I was stingy. I do a base application of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before spring growth starts, then topdress with urea after each cutting to push the regrowth. I irrigate 3-4 times through the season depending on rain — stevia doesn't like to dry out or the leaves get bitter and the buyer complains.

Pesticide — mostly I watch for aphids and some leaf-eating caterpillars. I spray maybe 2-3 times a season, nothing heavy. Weeds are the real problem so I use a pre-emergence herbicide in spring, then hand-weeding between rows. That's where the hired labor comes in — I can't do 35 mu of weeding with just my wife.

**For the cotton (15 mu):**
Planting around April 20-25, depending on soil temperature. I use Bt cotton seed — have for years now, it handles the bollworm so I spray less. Seed runs me about 70 yuan/mu for good hybrid seed.

Fertilizer on cotton — I do about 15 kg N/mu split across base and topdress at first bloom. Phosphorus 8 kg, potassium 8 kg, mixed in as compound fertilizer before planting. Irrigate twice usually — once before flowering and once during boll filling. If it's a dry year I might do a third.

Pesticide for cotton is the headache. Even with Bt, I still spray for aphids, spider mites, plant bugs — maybe 5-6 sprays through the season. Last year aphids were bad in July and I had to spray twice in two weeks. That stuff adds up.

The hardest part is picking. With just two of us, I can't pick 15 mu fast enough, so I hire 3-4 neighbors to help during the picking weeks. That's the biggest cost on cotton besides fertilizer.

**What I'm watching:**
- Stevia buyer price — if the contract price holds I'm in good shape. If it drops 20% I'll think about shifting more area back to cotton next year.
- Fertilizer prices — urea went up last year and it hurt. I already bought my base fertilizer in early spring when the price was lower.
- Labor — my regular hired workers are getting older too. Hiring is harder every year and the daily wage keeps going up.

I don't try to push for maximum yield. I try to get a solid crop, keep my input costs under control, and have cash left over at the end of the season. That's how I think about it.
